title: DeepSeek-V3.2 (Chat)
name: DeepSeek-V3.2 (Chat)
description: DeepSeek-V3.2 (Chat) is the family’s production chat variant and the first DeepSeek-V3.2 release to integrate thinking directly into tool-use while still supporting non-thinking chat paths.

best_for: General production chat with reasoning-aware behavior.
Tool-using agents that need thinking in tool-use.
Self-hosted high-capacity deployments that can absorb frontier-model memory and serving cost.
avoid_for: Single-GPU or low-memory deployments of the full checkpoint.
Workloads that require officially published hidden size, layer count, or training token counts before approval.
Environments that cannot support the model’s long-context memory and throughput demands.
engineering_snapshot.recommended_use_case: Use as the primary DeepSeek chat endpoint when you need one model to cover chat, mixed reasoning, and tool-using agents with official open-weight availability.
deployment_risks: Interconnect and Expert Parallel network layout scaling bottlenecks on standard cluster nodes.
Context window parsing latency and state overhead when mixing thinking and non-thinking chat templates.
failure_modes: Tokenizer mismatch and tool-call template formatting errors if custom encoding helpers are ignored.
OutOfMemory (OOM) failures under high concurrency without proper KV-cache sharding.
common_mistakes: Treating V3.2 as a drop-in generic chat model, bypassing the custom prompt/encoding paths.
Attempting single-GPU serving without planning high-speed interconnect and sharded tensor parallelism.
operational_notes: DeepSeek-V3.2 introduces “thinking in tool-use,” so production inference must handle both reasoning and non-reasoning paths instead of treating the model as a plain chat checkpoint.

The official release positions V3.2 as the balanced daily-driver model, while the API-only Speciale variant is reserved for deeper reasoning; this makes V3.2 the operational default for production chat + agent systems.

Use BF16 or FP8-capable infrastructure when possible, since the official checkpoint exposes BF16 and F8_E4M3 tensor types and the community recipes emphasize sparse-attention efficiency for long-context serving.

The official model card includes custom encoding helpers rather than a Jinja chat template, so integration code should follow the provided encoding/parse utilities instead of assuming a standard template path.

Variant differentiation (Identity): DeepSeek-V3.2 (Chat) is the family’s production chat variant and the first DeepSeek-V3.2 release to integrate thinking directly into tool-use while still supporting non-thinking chat paths.
Variant differentiation (File Formats): Safetensors format is officially published, while GGUF/AWQ/GPTQ and Apple Silicon MLX/ONNX formats are Not Published in official checkpoints.
Variant differentiation (Hardware Requirements): Community serving profiles target H100/H200/B200-class servers as the baseline for the full checkpoint.
Variant differentiation (Downloads): Canonical download paths include official Hugging Face repositories and DeepSeek release announcements.
Variant differentiation (Runtime Compatibility): vLLM recipes explicitly document DeepSeek-specific tool-call and tokenization paths, whereas edge llama.cpp features community conversions.
Variant differentiation (Deployment): integration of thinking mode directly into tool-use workflows sets V3.2 apart from earlier text-only or reasoning-only siblings.
Variant differentiation (License): MIT License allows very broad open-source utilization including modification, redistribution, and commercial deployment without active constraints.
Variant differentiation (Status): officially released production checkpoint targeted at robust structured reasoning.
